clue.text: Substitute with mission to keep record

indicators.note: to keep means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: a mission is a duty or task you are charged with
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A stand-in is sent on an assignment to safeguard some important document.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputy is someone who acts as a stand-in for another person.

clue.text: Stop in Antipodes is terrific

indicators.note: in says the answer is concealed within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A halt in Australasia is marvellous.
explanation.definitionFit: To desist is to cease doing something, to stop.

clue.text: Widespread hysteria taking over crowd

indicators.note: taking means the word for hysteria takes in the other pieces

parts.note: panic is wild hysteria or alarm
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
to ram or cram is to crowd in

explanation.surface: Mass panic sweeps over a throng of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A panoramic view is wide and sweeping, broad in scope.

clue.text: Harry is wrong about soldiers

indicators.note: about means the word for wrong goes round the other piece

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
men are soldiers, as opposed to officers

explanation.surface: A man named Harry is mistaken about the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a name; it is the verb meaning to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry is to harass persistently, to torment.

clue.text: Set off ambush reversed in action

indicators.note: in means the reversed piece sits inside the word for action

parts.note: a deed is an act or action

indicators.note: reversed means the word for ambush is read backwards

parts.note: to trap someone is to ambush them

explanation.surface: A trap is triggered when an ambush goes wrong during combat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set off' reads as triggering a trap, but it means left; 'reversed' gives PART for the word inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To have set off on a journey is to have left; both are past-tense verbs of leaving.

clue.text: Greek god is angry when upset

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: sore means angry or aggrieved

explanation.surface: A Greek deity is furious when thrown into turmoil.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love.

clue.text: Former politician remains controlling left

indicators.note: controlling means holding the other piece within it

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning
to quit is to leave, so left can mean quit

explanation.surface: An ex-politician still in charge of the left wing.
explanation.definitionFit: H. H. Asquith was a Liberal British prime minister from 1908 to 1916.

clue.text: Some advocate ether for their extraction?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people recommend anaesthetic before a dentist pulls something.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentists extract molars and incisors, the things the clue says are pulled.

clue.text: Detective's men reportedly providing cover

indicators.note: reportedly signals that what is spoken sounds like the entry

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector, so a DI's guys are the detective's men

explanation.surface: An inspector's team supply camouflage for an undercover operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A disguise conceals identity; cover is a false identity used to hide.

clue.text: Soldier's opening door for lookout

indicators.note: opening picks out the first letter of the word that precedes it

parts.note: a door is an entry or way in

explanation.surface: A soldier opens a door to keep watch outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry is a guard posted to keep watch, a lookout.

clue.text: Wins playground game, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals a word that sounds like the spoken one

parts.note: conkers is a children's game played with horse chestnuts on strings

explanation.surface: A child triumphs at a schoolyard game, as people report.
explanation.walkthrough: CONKERS is a British schoolchildren's game: each player swings a horse chestnut on a string to smash the other's.
explanation.definitionFit: To conquer is to overcome or defeat, so both mean triumphs over.

clue.text: Officer material with barnet oddly cut

parts.note: serge is a hard-wearing twilled fabric

indicators.note: oddly cut says the odd-numbered letters of the following word are removed, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: Someone's hair (barnet) is chopped unevenly using some fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: BARNET is Cockney rhyming slang for hair (Barnet Fair); here it is only letters, leaving A, N, T.
explanation.definitionFit: A sergeant is a non-commissioned officer in the army or police.

clue.text: Perhaps one could be less sensitive

definitions.meaning: one is an example of a numeral or figure
comparative of numb: having less feeling

explanation.surface: Someone might grow a bit desensitised.
explanation.definitionFit: One is an example of a figure; numb plus -er means more lacking feeling.

clue.text: Occasionally veils a Hindu god

indicators.note: occasionally means taking only every other letter of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A Hindu deity is sometimes depicted veiled.
explanation.definitionFit: Vishnu is one of the principal deities of Hinduism, the preserver.

clue.text: Squirm beside sweetheart embracing Romeo

indicators.note: embracing means the outer pieces hug the next one inside

parts.note: with means alongside or beside
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter

explanation.surface: Wriggling next to a lover who is hugging a Romeo.
explanation.definitionFit: To writhe is to twist the body about, to squirm.

clue.text: Crooked impostor has me for change

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dishonest fraud swaps someone for the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A metamorphosis is a complete transformation of form or nature.

clue.text: Dock worker to deserve getting fired

indicators.note: fired suggests being blasted apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A docker deserves to be sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: A stevedore loads and unloads ships at port.

clue.text: Male resists changing fancy woman

indicators.note: changing means altering the order of these letters

explanation.surface: A man fights off becoming involved with a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancy woman is an old-fashioned term for a man's lover outside marriage.

clue.text: Certain to be clean isn't bad

indicators.note: bad suggests something spoiled or wrong, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone is sure that being dirty is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beyond dispute is sure and undeniable.

clue.text: Atmosphere with English spirit lifted country

indicators.note: lifted in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: air is the atmosphere
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A national mood, boosted by English gin.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigeria is a country in West Africa.

clue.text: Pub anger leads to assault

parts.note: a bar is a pub
rage is fierce anger

explanation.surface: Fury in a tavern ends in violence.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrage is a heavy bombardment, a sustained attack.

clue.text: Very large quarry for hawk

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, very large in clothing sizes
quarry is prey that is hunted

explanation.surface: A predatory bird hunts some enormous target.
explanation.definitionFit: An osprey is a fish-eating bird of prey, often called the fish hawk.

clue.text: Still husband has strong exterior

indicators.note: exterior says the word for strong forms the outside around the other piece

parts.note: tough means strong and resilient

explanation.surface: A spouse remains, with a hardy outer shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Still and the answer are both adverbs meaning nevertheless or however.

clue.text: Command of royal decree exempts royals initially

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: An edict from the crown frees members of the royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: A command is an instruction given with authority, a directive.

clue.text: Brave nobleman in iron shackles, gutted

indicators.note: in places the nobleman inside the following pieces

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
an earl is a British nobleman

indicators.note: gutted means the insides are removed, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: An aristocrat is held in iron fetters, utterly devastated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' looks like the nobleman's despair, but it empties shackles down to its two end letters (SS).
explanation.definitionFit: Brave and the answer both describe someone without fear, bold.

clue.text: Border, say, of French brought up

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: eg (for example) is signalled by say
de is French for of

explanation.surface: A frontier, for instance, raised by the French.
explanation.definitionFit: A border is the boundary or rim of something.

clue.text: Place incredibly loaded with hidden gold

indicators.note: with hidden means the next piece is concealed inside the anagram
incredibly suggests something beyond belief, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: A spot fabulously rich, with treasure buried in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incredibly' rearranges the six letters of loaded into ELDADO; heraldic gold slips in after the third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary city of gold sought by conquistadors is the archetypal place of riches.

clue.text: Taste is rancid swallowing a volume

indicators.note: swallowing means the word for rancid takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: rancid food has gone sour

explanation.surface: Food tastes off after someone gulps down a book.
explanation.definitionFit: To relish or enjoy the flavour of something is to taste it fully.

clue.text: Flag ship carries Queen

indicators.note: carries means the ship holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: a steamer is a steamship
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A banner flies from the vessel transporting the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow pennant or ribbon flown from a mast is a kind of flag.

clue.text: Thin imbibing first of miracle cure

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so one piece takes the other inside

parts.note: reedy means thin and slender like a reed

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A frail patient drinks in the beginnings of a miraculous treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy is a treatment that heals, a cure.
